shape.description: What this device can see of its own health and the network's replication, reported through the network's own feed rather than to a collector. There is no endpoint and nothing phones home: a beat is an entry in this artifact's feed, so it reaches an operator the same way every other entry does — by being a member of the network they are a member of. Two things to write against. Every read here is eventually consistent for the reason platform:feed states: it merges the members this device can currently reach, so a fully partitioned member is absent rather than reported broken, and absence is the one fault this artifact cannot distinguish from a switched-off machine. And the coverage is partial by construction — call limits() and render what it names, because some of what an operator will ask about is not reachable from inside a realm and answering it with zero would be worse than not answering. What is reachable depends on the ports this network bound, which is why limits() is a call and not a document.

operations.name: beat
operations.description: Append one census of what this device can currently see. The only operation here that writes anything, and it takes no argument on purpose: a beat carrying a caller's string would put text this artifact did not author into an append-only log that replicates to every member. Suppressed when the census is identical to the last one this device wrote AND that beat is younger than this instance's beat floor. The floor is the whole of why a currency reading is possible: pure content-addressed suppression means a healthy member writes nothing, which makes a member that is fine and a member this device stopped replicating with produce byte-identical feeds, so no reading over the feed can separate them. Past the floor an unchanged census is written again — the same numbers, deliberately — so that a member's silence is falsifiable. A quiet fleet therefore grows its feed on time as well as on change, bounded at one entry per member per floor; a network that will not pay that sets the floor to zero, gets the old behaviour, and gets a limits() row saying currency is unanswerable there.

returns.description: What was written, or why nothing was

wrote.description: Whether an entry was appended. False means the census had not changed, which is the healthy case

seq.description: The sequence number in this device's own log, or null when nothing was written

reach.description: How many roster members this device holds anything from, this beat

roster.description: How many members the signed roster names

operations.name: local
operations.description: This device's own replication health, first-person. Computed from the signed roster and from what has actually arrived, so it is the one reading here that does not depend on another member being reachable — which makes it the reading to trust when the fleet view is thin.

returns.description: What this device holds, against what the network says exists

roster.description: Members the signed roster names, this device included

reached.description: Members this device holds at least one entry from. Monotone by construction — a replicated block stays on disk, so a member counted here once is counted here forever, however long ago it arrived. That is the count this field has always named and it is not the answer to "am I falling behind"; peers[].age is

silent.description: Roster members this device has received nothing from, sorted by key

peers.description: Every roster member and what this device holds from it, sorted by key

of.description: One member of the network, and what this device currently holds from it

device.description: The member's device key, z-base32, as feed entries carry it

seq.description: The highest sequence number this device holds from that member, or -1 when nothing from it has ever arrived

beats.description: How many of that member's health beats have reached this device

silent.description: Whether that member is in the signed roster and has sent this device nothing at all. Silence is not the same as failure — see limits

age.description: Milliseconds on THIS device's clock since this device last watched that member's log get longer, or null when it has not watched it move at all. The one reading here that answers "am I falling behind on this member": silent and seq answer whether anything ever arrived, which is permanent once true, and this answers when something last did. Never computed from the writer's timestamp — that is another device's unchecked clock and platform:feed says never to trust it — so it is a duration measured entirely here and is comparable across the members of one reading and not across devices. Null is not zero and not a large number: it means this instance has not seen the log move since it started, which lasts up to one beat floor after a zone restart. And it is only as informative as the beat floor the writing member is running: a member that never writes cannot be observed to have stopped, which is why suppression expires.

degraded.description: Whether any roster member is silent. A one-field answer for a caller that only wants to know whether to look closer

operations.name: fleet
operations.description: Every member's most recent beat that has reached this device. This is the answer to "replication is failing for 10% of consumers": a member whose own beat says it reaches 2 of 20 is reporting its own partial failure, and that report arrives as long as it can reach anybody. What it cannot show is a member that reaches nobody, because that member's report reaches nobody either.

returns.description: The fleet as the beats that got here describe it

reporting.description: Members whose beat has reached this device

worst.description: The lowest reach any reporting member claims, as a count of members; null when nobody has reported

members.description: One row per reporting member, worst reach first, then by key

of.description: One member's own account of what it can see

reach.description: How many members it said it holds anything from

roster.description: How many members its roster named when it wrote the beat

faults.description: How many first-person faults it reported in that beat

at.description: That member's own clock when it wrote the beat, as platform:feed carries it on the entry. A display hint and nothing else: it is that device's clock, nothing checks it, and it is never a sort key nor the input to any duration here

age.description: Milliseconds on THIS device's clock since this device last watched that member's log get longer, or null when it has not watched it move. The field to alert on, where at is the field to display — this one is measured here, so it is the only one of the two that means the same thing on every device reading it. See the same field on local().peers for what null means and why it is not zero

rosterDiffers.description: Whether that member counted a different number of roster members than this device does. Two members folding the same signed log agree on its size, so a difference means one of them is acting on a log it has not re-read — which is a staleness this device can see from outside and the stale device cannot see from inside

silent.description: Roster members that have never reported a beat here, sorted by key

operations.name: faults
operations.description: Faults this device observed about itself, as codes. First-person only: a fault is something that happened to this instance's own calls, never something inferred about somebody else. The wording of what went wrong is deliberately not here — see the code vocabulary, and the kernel's device-local journal for the fuller reason.

returns.description: One row per code seen, most recent first

of.description: A fault this device observed first-person, as a code from a closed vocabulary

code.description: What went wrong, from a fixed list — never a message, because a message is a string this artifact did not write

count.description: How many times this device has seen it since the counters were last written

at.description: When this device last saw it, by its own clock. A display hint, never a sort key across devices

operations.name: diagnostics
operations.description: What the kernel wrote in this device's own diagnostic ring, by kind, read through platform:diagnostics. Two things to hold on to before using a number here, both of which the platform contract states at greater length. First, the scope: the ring is device-wide, not per-network, so these counts include events belonging to other networks this device has joined — which is why they are on their own call and why none of them is ever put into a beat. Second, a kind is now a category for most of these names and not for all of them. "zone" is exactly the number of instances whose thread died and "refused" is exactly the number of things this device turned down — a contract nothing satisfies, an instance nothing could deliver, a platform pin this runtime cannot meet, a network retired mid-session, a release below the anti-rollback floor — so some of what it counts is a defence working rather than a fault. "fetch" is failures only, which the platform contract promises rather than merely describes, and it reads zero on any device you can ask this question of: a fetch that fails takes the boot down before an artifact runs, so the zero means this device came up and not that nothing ever failed. "served" is the other half of that split, a release that did arrive from a member rather than its author. "network" is the one name left that is several questions at once — unreachable, unresolved, not yet admitted, a moved pin, an expired wait, a fold that moved on — and is not a count of any one of them. When the port is not bound this answers observed false and no counts at all, rather than zeroes.

returns.description: The device's own diagnostic counts, or the fact that they were not reachable

observed.description: Whether the port answered. False means this network did not bind platform:diagnostics, or that the call was refused — and the two are distinguishable, because the second records a diagnostics-unreachable fault and the first records nothing. Read this before reading kinds: false with an empty list is "nobody measured", which is not the same claim as zero.

dropped.description: How many events the kernel's ring discarded to stay inside its bound since the process started. Above zero, every count below is a lower bound, because the ring drops entries and not counters. Zero when the port is not bound, which observed already says.

kinds.description: One row per kind the platform contract names, in its order, or empty when observed is false. Never partially filled: a caller reading a short list would be reading a vocabulary this release does not know rather than a device with fewer kinds of trouble.

of.description: One kind of diagnostic event and how many of it the kernel's ring still holds

kind.description: The kind, from the closed vocabulary platform:diagnostics declares — never a string this artifact or the kernel's journal composed. An entry whose kind the platform contract does not name is counted under "other" by the port itself. A name that is not shaped like a kind at all — too long, or outside lowercase letters, digits and hyphens — is collapsed into a single "unnamed" row here, counted rather than dropped. A kind this release has never heard of is reported under its own name, because a filter against a list held in an artifact would hide a newer runtime rather than a leak.

count.description: How many events of that kind the ring still holds. A lower bound whenever dropped is above zero

operations.name: limits
operations.description: What this artifact cannot observe, as data rather than as prose. Render it. A dashboard that shows zero for something nobody measured is the failure this operation exists to prevent, and the list shrinks on its own when the platform makes one of these reachable — which it has now done twice, so this list is shorter on a device that binds platform:diagnostics than on one that does not, and a caller comparing two devices is comparing two honest answers rather than one stale one. What is left on it is left for reasons no port can lift: a member that reaches nobody reports to nobody, and a fetch that fails destroys the device before the artifact that would report it exists.

returns.description: One row per thing an operator will ask for and this artifact cannot answer

subject.description: What is not observed, in the words the roadmap uses for it

observed.description: How much of it is observed: none, or partial

because.description: Why it is not reachable from inside a realm, in one sentence

covered.description: Where the fact does exist on this device, for whoever is standing at it

config.description: How much of a log this instance folds, and how long it may stay quiet

maxMembers.description: The most members whose beats are folded per call. A bound rather than a preference: a monitor must not become the reason a device is slow.

beatFloor.description: The longest an unchanged census may go on suppressing a beat, in milliseconds. Five minutes when a network does not say — lib/resident.js re-derives on that clock, so freshness finer than it is not available anyway. Past the floor a device with nothing new to say writes the same census again, which is what makes a member going quiet mean something: with pure content-addressed suppression a healthy member and one this device stopped replicating with produce identical feeds. Zero or less switches the floor off and restores that older behaviour, bounding the feed by change alone at the cost of any currency reading; limits() on such a device says so.
